title: Sidera Caeli – Devlog #3 | Inventory, Hangars, Ship Loadouts, Mining & Refining
author: danidomen
selftext:
Here's my third devlog for Sidera Caeli, my browser-based multiplayer space game!

I've been working on quite a few new systems, including inventory and trading, private hangars with ATC management, ship customization, and a complete mining loop, from scanning and fracturing asteroids to unloading, refining, and trading materials. I've also added mining contracts and improved the ship retrieval effects.

Everything is still very much a work in progress. The game is being developed from scratch with AI assistance, but entirely based on my own ideas, specifications, and quality control throughout the development process. No reverse engineering of any existing game or software has been involved whatsoever. Many of the current 3D assets are still AI-generated placeholders.

Just wanted to share the progress. There's also a free public testbed available for anyone interested in trying it out and hopefully get some feedback!

**Previous devlogs:**

* **Devlog #2:** [Transit, Squads, Hacking, Cargo Physics & More!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BCxwWFDGW2s)
* **Devlog #1:** [I Added an AI-Generated Ship to My Three.js Multiplayer Game in 5 Minutes!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t74Rj9U2pks)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/danidomen could you add more about how AI fit into your development process? Under Rule 4, promotional posts need to contribute something by discussing how the game was actually made. Otherwise the sub gets buried in ads. If there's no update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: danidomen
replies.body:
Edited and added to the post, but basically everything that shows the video in movement, is thanks to AI:  
**AI has played a significant role in this release, particularly through Codex-Astra**, helping me turn specifications into working code, integrate different systems, debug issues, and iterate on performance and functionality. My focus has been on defining the architecture, designing the mechanics, writing detailed specifications, and testing and reviewing the results, with particular attention to quality, performance, and security.

Regarding the 3D assets, I have subscriptions to both Meshy and Tripo. The mining ship shown in this video was generated with Tripo, as it gave me better results in this particular case. Honestly, it's mostly trial and error between the two, and I couldn't really say which one is better overall. Lately, though, I've been getting better results with Tripo, even if it comes at a slightly higher cost.
